items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Edward Clem' (Clemson) extensively as a bandleader he played with, but the name 'Clemson' itself is only mentioned by the Interviewer in the line 'That's what Clemson said.' The Interviewee does not use the name 'Clemson' nor explicitly link the name 'Clemson' to the perso

ctx.x: He was out every week. Yeah. He was on that road. Hammond, Ponchatoula, Bugalusa. I've seen the time we'd go to Bugalusa and stay, four nights out there playing. Yeah, Edward Clem. He was a good trumpet player. And he had Willie Warner, was playing clarinet. Old fella called Willie Warner. And Sugar, fella called Sugar. I already know his first name. We always did call him Sugar, you know. Trombone. That was a vowel trombone he had. Didn't have no sliders out. And so we, let's see, let's see how many more we had.…

Yeah. He said, oh, they didn't want him no more. They got tired of him. So he said, we're going to hire you. We want you on the bass. He said, you can play and shoot us. And he was living up here on Padilla right there by Ramport, upstairs there.
